title: Jack’s General Store: Developing a Inventory Mangement System
text:
This project involved designing and implementing a relational inventory management system for a simulated small retail business using SQL and Oracle APEX. The system enables inventory tracking, product management, allergen monitoring, and reporting functionalities through an interactive web-based application. The project applied database design principles, normalization techniques, and user-centered interface development to address common inventory management challenges faced by small businesses ## Project Deliverables

Create a database schema for the inventory management system, including tables for products, inventory, and sales.
Provide a user-friendly interface for store employees to add, update, and delete product information.
Implement a reporting system that allows the store manager to generate reports on sales and inventory trends.

title: Jack’s General Store: Developing a Inventory Mangement System
text:
Technical Design and Implementation
The system was built using Oracle SQL and Oracle APEX and included: - Product table - Inventory table - Sales table - Allergen table - Product-Allergen junction table The database design enforced referential integrity through primary and foreign key relationships while supporting inventory tracking and reporting functionalities.

title: Jack’s General Store: Developing a Inventory Mangement System
text:
Project Assumptions

10 data projects are provided for this demonstration
All data constraints and primary keys are met and assumed to be unique or auto-generated
Automated data storage is provided when the new product is recorded in the new product intake, including allergens and inventory.
Products can have multiple allergens. Inventory is assumed to reference one product.
Queries are valid and assumed
The business manager must manually change any allergen to any product by filling out a new allergen form and a new product intake, then the inventory dashboard is recorded based on recency.
The inventory table records all inventory transactions, meaning all products are recounted on each inventory-recording day.

title: Jack’s General Store: Developing a Inventory Mangement System
text:
Project Limitations

One technical challenge involved automating updates between the product-allergen junction table and related inventory forms within Oracle APEX. To maintain data integrity, an alternative workflow was implemented that allowed managers to manually update allergen information while ensuring the inventory dashboard reflected the most recent records.
This challenge strengthened my understanding of many-to-many database relationships, junction tables, and form automation within database-driven applications.

title: Early Hearing Detection and Intervention Program Policy Analysis: Expanding Beyond the Medical Perspective
text:
The purpose of the Early Hearing Detection and Intervention is to prevent more cases of not getting treatment for hearing loss; however, deaf community members and scholars have argued that the program is not designed to accomplish language development, since it heavily focuses on the medical perspective of hearing loss.
Early intervention programs have become a vital social program for all infants, including the Deaf and Hard of Hearing infants, ensuring developmental and cognitive milestones. Findings will inform policy design and implementaiton of the Early Hearing Detection and Intervention program using the California’s Language Equality and Acquisition for Deaf Kids (LEAD-K) framework to ensure that the program is designed to support language development for Deaf and Hard of Hearing infants.
To ensure that this project meets the requirements of “Honors Option” for the RIT Honors Program, the goals of the Honors Options are to engage in scholarly discosure and dissemination with the RIT community, to enchance my understanding of social policy and inequities, the following project deliverables will be completed to meet the requirements of the Honors Option.

title: Emma M. Kane
text:
Thanks for stopping by!
I work as a Research Assistant at the NTID Research Center on Culture and Language at Rochester Institute of Technology.
My research interests focus on using data to improve educational outcomes for Deaf and Hard of Hearing students.
My current project with the NTID Research Center on Culture and Language aims to develop standardized assessment tools in American Sign Language to evaluate and screen for Alzheimer’s disease and dementia among Deaf and Hard of Hearing older adults. Learn more about our work here.
Connect with me on LinkedIn.

title: Service
text:
University Service

NTID Student Representative, RIT Einsenhart Award Committee — Oct 2026 - Present
Role and Responsibilities: Nominated to serve as the student representative for the two prestigious university-wide teaching awards at RIT, the Eisenhart Award and the Provost Award. The committee was responsible for reading instructor evaluations, participating in classroom observations, and holding meetings to determine which candidates to recommend to the Provost for the awards.
Student Representative, NTID President Search Commitee — Feb 2025 - July 2025
Role and Responsibilities: Represented student perspectives in the national search and selection process for the NTID President. The committee was responsible for determining finalists to recommend to the RIT President for the NTID President position.
RIT SG Representative, RIT University Council — Sept 2024 - Dec 2024
Role and Responsibilities: Represented RIT SG in the university-wide decision-making process. University Council is an integral part of the shared governance model of leadership at RIT; the council is reponsible of reviewing student feedback, providing recommendations to the RIT President, and making decisions on university-wide policies.

title: Service
text:
Community Involvement

Founding Executive Board Member, RIT/NTID Deaf Business Council — 2026-Present
Currently serving as a founding executive board member of the RIT/NTID Deaf Business Council, a student organization that aims to provide a safe and inclusive space for RIT/NTID Deaf and Hard of Hearing students who are interested in business. This organization aims to provide networking opportunities, programming, and events to support the professional development of Deaf and Hard of Hearing students who are interested in Business at RIT.
Executive Board Member, RIT/NTID Cross-Registered Student Advisory Board — 2024-2026
Served in different roles for the RIT/NTID Cross-Registered Student Advisory Board, serving all Deaf and Hard of Hearing students enrolled in Bachleor’s and Master’s programs at RIT who recieve services from NTID. The advisory board is reponsible for creating a saafe and inclusive space for all DHH students to voice their concerns and provide feedback about their student experience at RIT. The board also provides events and programming to support the DHH student community at RIT.
Cross-Registered Senator, RIT Student Government - 2024-2025 Elected to serve as the Cross-Registered Senator for all Deaf and Hard of Hearing students enrolled in Bachleor’s and Master’s programs at RIT who recieve services from NTID. The senator is responsible for representing the student voice of the DHH student community at the Student Govenment meetings and commitees, advocating for the needs of the DHH student community, and providing feedback to RIT SG on how to improve the student experience for DHH students at RIT.
